scope: Lark self-send, notification and member/tool configuration first family; no further provider-family expansion
measurement_notes: Before and after use the same 54 top-level test selection, integration tag, count=1 and default Go parallel setting with the existing four fixture slots. Commands run sequentially.

The working directory also has unrelated concurrent development and external test processes; this is not a controlled whole-repository performance baseline or a causal diagnosis of elapsed-time variation.

Fixture tracing was temporary and removed. Counts retain real production verification and native child processes; native trace counts start events in disposable Python fixtures, including invocations killed before exit.
Lark account time includes account save and production verification/native CLI. Python body timing is not native process wall time and is not reported as such.
Phase sums and slot seconds are cumulative work, not additive command wall time. Explicit close/reopen and nested service process cleanup can remain in flow.

Before service tracing covered 82 legacy CLI fixtures, excluding the three existing Lark-only entrypoint fixtures; after service tracing covers all 85. Do not treat those service totals as a paired speedup.

Final source removes tracing, restores the legacy CLI helper body exactly and replaces temporary provider-only aliases with explicit WithMembers calls; selected room shapes and test assertions are unchanged.
No business tests, failure boundaries, fsync, permission checks, build tags, timer values or fixture slot limits were removed or relaxed.

work_removed.member_count_basis: 85 Lark fixtures with three members before, one additional three-member cross-Room fixture. After, 78 single-member plus seven two-member Lark fixtures and one additional single-member Room. Counts describe initial membership materialization, not DSH model launches.
